review_material.assessment: The source packet provides a complete experimental and theoretical description of the unitary almost-Mathieu operator (UAMO) and its non-Hermitian extension (PUAMO) realized via single-photon quantum walks. The selected quantitative cluster focuses on the Lyapunov exponent L_lambda1_lambda2_eta of the PUAMO, given by L = max(0, log(lambda_0) - 2*pi*|eta|) with lambda_0 = lambda_2*(1+lambda_1')/(lambda_1*(1+lambda_2')). Two claims are built for the private regimes eta=0 and eta=0.1, sharing public controls lambda_1 and lambda_2 in [0.2,0.67] and the common readout lyapunov_exponent. The source reports the full parameter-space phase scans for the Hermitian (eta=0) and non-Hermitian (eta=0.1) cases, and the Lyapunov formula is explicitly given in the supplementary material. The extraction captures the central quantitative relation with all structural constants as named, anchored parameters. The source contains internal inconsistencies in the PT-threshold wording: the main text states eta_PT = -log(lambda_0) (line 125) and Methods states eta = -log(lambda_0) (line 211), while the supplementary dual exponent formula at line 359 and the reported numeric value 0.119 for lambda_1=0.25, lambda_2=0.5 (line 152) imply eta_PT = log(lambda_0)/(2*pi). Additionally, supplementary prose at lines 366-367 places turning points at nonsensical eta=+/-lambda_0 and states thresholds using log(lambda_0) without the required 2*pi, and line 227 says delocalization starts as soon as 2*pi*eta>0 immediately after stating localization persists while 2*pi*eta<L. These are prose errors that do not affect the selected Lyapunov equations, which are internally consistent and supported by the reported 0.119 value. Therefore case_authoring_ready is set to true.

review_material.paper_scope: The paper reports the first experimental realization of the unitary almost-Mathieu operator (UAMO) and its non-Hermitian extension (PUAMO) using single-photon quantum walks. It observes metal-insulator transitions in the Hermitian limit, PT-symmetry-breaking transitions, and a novel spectral transition where all quasienergies become purely imaginary. The selected quantitative cluster focuses on the Lyapunov exponent L_lambda1_lambda2_eta, which quantifies the inverse localization length and is given by L = max(0, log(lambda_0) - 2*pi*|eta|) with lambda_0 = lambda_2*(1+lambda_1')/(lambda_1*(1+lambda_2')). Two claims are built for the private regimes eta=0 and eta=0.1, sharing public controls lambda_1 and lambda_2 in [0.2,0.67] and the common readout lyapunov_exponent.

anchors.support: The significance of the Lyapunov exponent L is that it quantifies the inverse localization length of solutions to the secular equation
This can be inferred from the Lyapunov exponent L_lambda1_lambda2_Phi of the model, which describes the average decay of eigenstates
